title: The power of language models

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: it's still the interaction between people that makes us think better. It feels now that language models, they have all that information. They have

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: of people talking with one another. They have all these moments

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: people also learn. But they have a sheer unlimited number of those. So...

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: that sense, you can say the way you think, in large parts, you learn it by talking. But if the way you learn by talking,

limitations: Automatic ASR and diarization; no human audio audit or calibrated identity probability.
Rhys labels use only the upstream rhys_speaker_id; machine identity assignment can be wrong.
Other speaker IDs are local anonymous labels, not inferred guest names. Unknown/overlap is retained.
A speaker can quote someone else; transcript statements are not automatically Rhys beliefs.
Public privacy screening omits flagged turn text and can miss sensitive context.
Canonical text transcribes the declared RSS or YouTube recording. Corresponding editions are aliases, not identical recordings.
